title: SALTY MAKES SWEET GOODBYE
text:
As 2025 ended, so did a unique arrangement between two local restaurants under the same roof on Watson Avenue.
Salty Restaurant & Wine Bar, the Mediterranean style eatery that has operated inside the Village Hearth Bakery since February 2024, has departed. Owner Noah Cain was appreciative of the bakery’s owners, Lindsay and Stephanie Haigh, for allowing him to use their space.
“They’ve been great,” he said. “Our customers have been great. The community has been great.”
Salty served its final dinner on New Year’s Eve. Cain, who operates Salty with his wife, Alex, said the decision to depart was amicable.
“We want to find our own space,” he said. “We want to be able to grow the experience of Salty.”
Cain said it was an “incredible opportunity” to work with the Haighs. As the Cains search for their next site, he said the two-year tenure at Village Hearth has taught them “what we want to keep bringing to the community.”
“I think we’ve learned a lot about our dining experience at Salty,” he said.
Lindsay Haigh noted the crossover in customers. Some would visit the bakery for breakfast, then return to Salty for dinner.
“I think people really enjoyed it,” she said. “The fact that we’re able to facilitate something new in the community, and give back to the community, was the best part of it.”
Prior to opening Salty, Cain had been sous chef at the Coast Guard House in Narragansett and executive chef at the MainSail restaurant inside the Newport Marriott Hotel.
The Haighs met Cain after they purchased the bakery in 2021. Cain had stopped by the bakery for pizza and introduced himself to the owners. Soon after, he began helping in the kitchen.
“We naturally became friends,” Stephanie Haigh said.
Salty first arrived at the Village Hearth in February 2024. The trial period was a success with Cain selling out his dishes through that first winter and spring. This led to their transformation to a permanent fixture in July.
“The pop-up was sort of a starting point idea to see how our dining experience would come together,” Cain said. “It went really well.”
Cain described Village Hearth as a cozy space that served as a good learning experience. He learned what aspects of the restaurant worked, what they want to continue using, and what they would do in terms of style, decoration and menu once they find their own space.
The dishes at Salty when they were at Village Hearth included braised lamb, bluefin tuna crudo, scallops a la plancha and fluke from Point Judith.
The menu rotated often, but Cain said the staples kept customers coming back regularly. Stephanie Haigh mentioned her favorite “not-so-salty” item, the chocolate mousse.
Cain said his favorite memories from Salty’s time at Village Hearth were the staff meetings and family meals that were held an hour before service began. That’s when they would comb the guest list, describe the menu and eat together.
“I think that was, and will always be, a very important and enjoyable part of the day,” Cain said. “I think that formed so much for our staff, and for me, and for the people that we’re working with. It helped sort of elevate the experience that we’d give to our guests.”
Lindsay Haigh said Salty departing Village Hearth was “built in from the beginning.”
“We stuck to the plan that we all originally went with, which was a two-year partnership,” she said. “It came to its natural conclusion with Noah knowing he wanted to move on.”
While Salty is looking for its own permanent location, the restaurant will continue to offer its food in Jamestown. People can order online at saltywinebar.com for pickup Thursdays through Sundays at Central Baptist Church.
“We’re continuing on a different scale,” he said.
The meals-to-go menu currently includes braised lamb shanks, smoked mackerel spread, vegetable soup, baked pasta, roasted root vegetables and almond cake.
While Cain does not yet have a location, Jamestown remains an option if a feasible site was to become vacant.
The Haighs said they do not plan to repeat a similar partnership with another guest chef. If the Cains have trouble finding a location, however, Salty could make a temporary seasonal return to Watson Avenue in 2026.
“We’re really happy about being able to work with Stephanie and Lindsay, and do something fun like that,” Cain said. “I certainly would be open to that.”
